text:
Jordan (Manager): quick runbook question  onboarding a new parent who asked about the exact paperwork/timelines for parental leave (state CA). they want to know when to submit, what docs/pay they'll get, and if they can stagger return.
Maya (People Ops): TL;DR: start paperwork 30 days before planned leave if possible. for CA: submit `FMLA-2026` + `CA-PDL` forms + medical certification. if shorter notice, still submit asap; we can process retroactively.
Lee (Eng): they asked about paid benefits while on leave. what's Redwood's top-up policy again?
Maya (People Ops): Redwood provides 12 weeks of company-paid parental top-up (after STD) for primary caregivers, prorated for part-time. top-up combined with state disability (SDI) and PFL: we coordinate payments so employee nets up to their base pay (subject to caps). include pay calendar note: state payments are disbursed ~2-3 weeks after claim.
Priya (Payroll): payroll note: to hit the payroll cutoff, forms + medical cert must be uploaded to the HR portal by the 5th of the month prior to leave start for that month's payroll cycle. if we receive later we'll do a retro adj but it may require a separate correction check. use expense code `PARENT-LEAVE` for any one-time reimbursements.
Jordan (Manager): what about staggered/part-time return (phased return)? can they split the 12 weeks or stretch it?
Maya (People Ops): yes we support phased returns. options: 1) reduced hours + pro-rated top-up for up to 12 weeks, or 2) request an extended unpaid leave window (up to 6 months) if they want to stretch bonding time. both require a written return-to-work plan signed by manager and People Ops.
HR Bot: https://hr.redwood.example/forms/FMLA-2026  FMLA filing portal.
Lee (Eng): also need to know equipment policy: do they keep laptop during leave?
Maya (People Ops): standard: employees keep company equipment during approved leave. if leave extends beyond 6 months, we may request periodic security checks and asset verification.
Priya (Payroll): benefits continuity: health premiums continue if employee is enrolled and premium deductions are active when leave starts. if unpaid leave later causes premium lapse, we offer COBRA options. 401(k): employee can still make contributions if on partial paid leave; match continues based on payroll eligibility.
Jordan (Manager): forms: is there a manager approval step or just People Ops?
Maya (People Ops): manager must confirm leave dates in the portal (approval step `Manager-Confirm`). People Ops does the benefits and payroll setup after manager confirmation.
Priya (Payroll): for CA-specific PFL claims remind them: the state portal will ask employer contact info and we will need the expected leave dates. encourage employee to start their claim themselves and cc payroll.
Maya (People Ops): checklist I'm attaching in-thread: 1) employee submits FMLA-2026 + CA-PDL via HR portal; 2) attach medical certification/BAA if required; 3) manager confirms dates in portal (Manager-Confirm); 4) People Ops approves and flags Payroll; 5) Payroll runs payment coordination (state + company top-up); 6) document phased-return plan if applicable; 7) update team runbook + backfill plan.
Jordan (Manager): good. any templated language I should use for the leave announcement to the team?
Maya (People Ops): yep, we have a short template: "[Name] will be on parental leave from [start] to [end]. Please direct day-to-day questions to [backup]. We'll update on-call rota." I'll DM the template.
Priya (Payroll): final thing: if the employee has travel booked that overlaps leave, travel reimbursements must be submitted before leave starts or they'll need manager pre-approval for reimbursement after the fact.
Lee (Eng): thanks all. I'll pass this to the engineer and copy the links.
Maya (People Ops): happy to help  ping me if you want me to walk through the portal with the employee.
HR Bot: Reminder: if FMLA-2026 is started and not completed within 7 days a People Ops rep will follow up via email.
Jordan (Manager): closing this thread; will post when filed. :white_check_mark:
